en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Chapter The Twenty-second Chapter
Discussion on the Condition of Repetition:
Is there no such thing as the condition of repetition? Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
"Bhikkhus, the destruction of life, when practiced, cultivated, and frequently repeated, leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, and leads to the sphere of hungry ghosts;
the lightest result of the destruction of life is that for one who has become human, it leads to a short lifespan"?
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, there is indeed some such thing as the condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya).
"There is no such thing as a condition by way of repetition"?
Yes, that is so.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Bhikkhus, taking what is not given, when practiced, cultivated, and frequently pursued, leads to rebirth in hell, leads to rebirth in the animal realm, and leads to rebirth in the sphere of hungry ghosts.
At the very least, for one who has become human, the result of taking what is not given is the ruin of wealth.
…pe… At the very least, for one who has become human, the result of sexual misconduct is the arising of enmity and hostility. …pe…
The lightest result of false speech is that it leads one who has become human to being falsely accused of something extraordinary.
… The lightest result of malicious speech is that it leads one who has become human to being divided from friends.
… The lightest result of harsh speech is that it leads one who has become human to hearing unpleasant sounds. …
“The lightest result of frivolous speech for one who has become a human being is that it leads to one’s speech not being respected.

The drinking of fermented and distilled liquors, monks, when indulged in … [as before] … the lightest result of drinking fermented and distilled liquors for one who has become a human being is that it leads to insanity.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes.
Then, in that case, is it the case that there is some condition of repetition?
Or is it the case that there is no condition of repetition?
“Yes, [it is so].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, wrong view, when practiced, developed, and cultivated, leads to rebirth in hell, leads to rebirth in the animal realm, and leads to rebirth in the sphere of hungry ghosts’?”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, there is indeed some condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya).
"There is no such thing as a condition by way of repetition"?
Yes, [you say].
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Wrong intention … wrong concentration,
bhikkhus, when practiced and cultivated … leads to the realm of hungry ghosts.
Is there such a sutta?
“Yes.
Well then, there is some condition of repetition;
is it not the case that there is no condition of repetition?
“Yes, [it is so].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, right view, when practiced, developed, and cultivated, has the Deathless as its ground, the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its consummation’?”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, there is indeed some condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya).
"There is no such thing as a condition by way of repetition"?
Yes, [you say].
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Right intention, bhikkhus, when practiced, developed, and cultivated extensively … right concentration,
bhikkhus, when practiced, developed, and cultivated extensively, has the Deathless as its destination, the Deathless as its final goal,
and the Deathless as its consummation. Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes.
In that case, there is indeed some condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya).
The discussion on the condition of repetition is concluded.
